lessons.culture: In Sanaani homes, greeting guests warmly with "7ayyak allah" is customary. The phrase "sharraft il-bayt" (you honored the house) is a warm way to welcome guests and acknowledge their visit.

lessons.culture: Sanaani meals are communal and hospitable. The phrase "bil-hana w ash-shifa" (enjoy your meal) is always said. Offering extra food shows warmth; turning it down politely is normal and acceptable. Spicy food is common in Yemeni cooking, and warning guests kindly is respectful. Desserts (halwiyyat) are always served after the main meal.

lessons.culture: In Sanaani culture, parting with guests is as warm as welcoming them. Saying goodbye never happens abruptly; there are always expressions of thanks and wishes for safe travels. "Tisbih 3ala khair" (sleep on goodness) is said to those leaving in the evening. Inviting guests to return soon is customary and sincere. Islamic expressions like "in shaa allah" (God willing) are natural in everyday speech.

lessons.culture: In Sana'a the fast is broken with dates, water and often قِشْر (qishr, a drink of coffee husks), with شَفُوت (shafoot, flatbread in spiced yoghurt) on the table; the men pray Maghrib, and only then comes the full meal. exercises.prompt: Complete: "_____ لِصَلَاة الْفَجْر." (I will wake you up for the dawn prayer.)

too_formal.feedback: "سأوقظك" is Fusha; in Sana'a say "شاصحّيك".

exercises.tip: "شا" marks what I will do.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "عَتْبَات عِنْدَنَا اللَّيْلَة، _____ مُشْكِلَة." (You'll stay the night with us, no problem.)

too_formal.feedback: "لا توجد مشكلة" is formal; say "مابش مشكلة".

exercises.tip: "مابش" is "there isn't".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "This is your room." (to a man)
exercises.tip: To a woman: "هذي غرفتش".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Where is the bathroom?"
Translate: "What time do you want to wake up?" (to a man)
exercises.tip: "تشتي" is "you want"; it is the same word to a woman, with "تصحي" after it.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Here are folded blankets in case you feel cold"?
options: حطيت لك فوط نظيفة فوق السرير

exercises.prompt: Which word means "towel"?
Put the words in order: "قوي / الله / أكرمتني / يكرمك".
exercises.tip: Start with the prayer "الله يكرمك".

challenge.title: Host a Guest
challenge.instructions: Create a conversation in Sanaani where you welcome a guest, offer them refreshment, invite them to dinner, and say goodbye warmly. Use at least one greeting phrase, one drink offer, one meal invitation, and one goodbye phrase from the lessons.
required_elements: A welcoming greeting (e.g. حَيَّاك اللَّه or أَهْلاً وَسَهْلاً)
An offer of food or drink (قَهْوَة وَلاَّ شَايْ, etc.)

dialogue.speaker: أَنْتَ
dialogue.english: Welcome! Come in.

dialogue.speaker: الضَّيْف
dialogue.english: God give you life, how are you?

dialogue.speaker: أَنْتَ
dialogue.arabic: تِمَام الْحَمْدُ لِلَّه. إِيش اللَّي تِشْتِي تِشْرَب؟
dialogue.transliteration: tamam al-7amdu lillah. eesh il-li tishti tishrab?
dialogue.english: Good, thank God. What would you like to drink?

dialogue.speaker: الضَّيْف
dialogue.english: Coffee, please.

dialogue.speaker: أَنْتَ
dialogue.arabic: تِمَام. تَفَضَّل عَلَى الْمَائِدَة، الْعَشِي جَاهِز
dialogue.english: Good. Please come to the table, dinner is ready.

dialogue.speaker: الضَّيْف
dialogue.english: Enjoy the meal.

dialogue.speaker: أَنْتَ
dialogue.english: Thanks for coming. Goodbye.
